subject.title: RFC: Period-based popularity for publishers, skills, and plugins

question: Should ClawHub fund a shared temporal-popularity data model for publishers, skills, and plugins before adding any Weekly or Monthly browse tabs?
rationale: The remaining work changes persistent statistics, attribution semantics, ranking behavior, and discovery UX; source-level implementation cannot safely choose those product contracts on its own.

options.title: Approve the shared foundation
options.body: Define a simple downloads-first V1 with event-time attribution, bounded daily rollups, and snapshot-pinned weekly/monthly leaderboards before UI work.

options.title: Limit the first release
options.body: Ship period popularity only for the entity family with an already-correct bounded data contract, and label the scope precisely rather than presenting it as cross-surface popularity.

options.title: Defer temporal discovery
options.body: Keep current all-time and existing trending surfaces until the data-model and discovery priorities warrant the storage and backfill investment.

recommendation.title: Approve the shared foundation
recommendation.body: Define a simple downloads-first V1 with event-time attribution, bounded daily rollups, and snapshot-pinned weekly/monthly leaderboards before UI work.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only evidenced participant with detailed ownership of the RFC’s tradeoffs; an assigned product owner can replace this routing if one is designated.
